To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shape of a disk galaxy's rotation curve can be used to determine the axis ratios of the underlying halo and that the dark matter halo of a disk galaxy can have a cuspier density profile than the Navarro, Fennk, White model.

the shape of rotation curves depends on the orientation of a disk with respect to the line of the sight, and that the shape of a rotation curve may differ from the shape of the dark matter density profile, and that the latter may not necessarily follow the NFW profile.

the shape of the dark mass profile of triaxial halos is inferred from rotation curves of disk galaxies with a significant scatter, which is not due to the scatter of dark mass profiles, but rather to the fact that the shape of rotation curves depends on the relative orientation of the disk with the line of sight and the halo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of disks embedded in CDM halos, with particular emphasis on the effects of halo tri-axiality.
the structure of disk galaxies in the context of the CDM model.
the dynamics and structure of disk galaxies embedded in dark matter halos.

the shape and amplitude of rotation curves in low surface brightness galaxies are not in conflict with the structure of Cdm halos.
the shape of the dark matter density profile is not directly observable in the rotation curves of disk galaxies.
the shape of the observed rotation curve is a poor indicator of the shape of the dark matter distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dark matter density distribution is not constrained by the shape of the observed rotation curve.
the rotation curve shape is not a good tracer of the dark matter density profile.
the rotation curves of disk galaxies in triaxial CDM halos are more complex than the rotation curve of a spherical halo with the same mass distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rotation curves of disks embedded in triaxial dark matter halos may not be a reliable probe of the structure of the dark matter.
the shape of the dark matter rotation curve is not necessarily a good indicator of the shape of the underlying density distribution.
the dark mass inferred from rotation curves is a function of the orientation of the line of sight relative to the halo axes.
